text:
maria: Hey team — Acme (tenant acme-prod) reporting sudden p99 spikes ~300-600ms starting 2026-02-18 10:05 UTC. They believe requests that should hit us-west are being routed via eu-west and back. No auth/billing errors from them, just high latency and occasional 502s. TraceID: rc-98765.

sam (acme): Confirmed. TraceID rc-98765, client IP 3.120.45.78. No token failures. It started right after your scheduled peering maintenance around 09:58 UTC.

anna: Can you paste the raw trace and traceroute output? Also which model/route are they hitting (we need route config).

maria: Pasting trace snippet and traceroute below. Route: /v1/generate -> route=prod-us-west-lowlatency (tenant override).

--- trace rc-98765 ---
root span: edge-proxy-us-west (start)
  child span: shard-proxy -> edge-eu-west (routed_via=eu-west1, fallback_reason=peer_pref_change) +420ms
  child span: edge-eu-west -> compute-us-west (return path) +110ms
--- end trace ---

--- traceroute from customer (to 54.23.12.11) ---
traceroute to edge-us-west.example.redwood (54.23.12.11), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  192.168.1.1 (192.168.1.1)  1.123 ms  0.987 ms  1.021 ms
 2  52.17.4.2 (52.17.4.2)  2.11 ms  2.07 ms  2.09 ms
 3  34.199.88.7 (34.199.88.7) eu-core  420.456 ms 420.301 ms 420.378 ms
 4  54.23.12.11 (54.23.12.11)  420.512 ms 420.430 ms 420.499 ms
--- end traceroute ---

kevin: I see this looks like traffic preferring our EU egress peer for that /24. We rolled a community tag change during the maintenance at 09:56 UTC that inadvertently increased preference for eu peer for a subset of ASN paths. Looks correlated.

anna: I attempted to reproduce from our us-west bastion. Repro steps below:

1) ssh bastion-us-west
2) curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer <test-token>" -H "X-Tenant-ID: acme-prod" "https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate?model=redwood-alpha"
3) grep X-Served-Region from headers

Result: X-Served-Region: eu-west-1 (expected us-west-2). Payload routing header shows route_decision: "fallback:peering-preference,elected_region:eu-west-1"

anna: Also ran an internal trace with sampling=100% and saw fallback_path triggered due to a mis-eval in capacity check: available_slots reported 0 for us-west lowlatency pool for ~2m due to a metric spike right at maintenance window. The routing logic then used peering preference and ended up sending to eu.

jordan: On-call here. I can push a tenant-level routing override to force region affinity while we fix the root cause. Deploying a temporary override for tenant acme-prod to prefer us-west and disable cross-region fallback for low-latency tier. Will monitor.

deploy-bot: deploy started by jordan: patch routing/overrides/2026-02-18/acme-override -> status: in_progress

sre-bot: alert: p99 for acme-prod decreased from 420ms to 55ms after override (monitoring).

maria: Customer confirmed improvement: "latency returned to normal after you applied the override, thanks" :thumbsup:

kevin: I'll open a networking ticket to rollback the community change and add a gating check to ensure we don't widen preference for cross-region peers during maintenance. Ticket NET-4721 created.

anna: Action items:
- kevin: rollback and post BGP diff + postmortem (NET-4721)
- anna: add unit/integration test to routing logic to simulate transient capacity zeros so fallback policy won't choose far region unless absolutely necessary
- jordan: keep override for acme-prod for now, schedule automatic revert after BGP rollback confirmed (no sooner than 6h)
- maria: follow up with customer EOD and share RCA draft

maria: Thanks team — logging the thread and moving to high priority RCA. If anyone captures PCAPs or tcpdump from customer-facing edge while the override was active, attach them here.

sam (acme): Thanks for the quick mitigation. We'll leave a contact open in case you need more info.

kevin: attaching short debug lines from BGP control plane (excerpt):
"2026-02-18T09:56:12Z BGP: update community set +local-pref:200 -> matched-prefix 54.23.12.0/24 -> applied to peer eu-peer-1"

maria: Last_message: setting follow-ups and assigning owners. Closing thread once NET-4721 has a fix and override is reverted.
